maya: quick read — I ran the cobalt-lite-8p3 onboarding sweep (int6 vs int8) across our consumer-chat slices. attached a short micro-slice summary + unit-econ. TL;DR: int6 cuts per-call token cost ~35% and reduces p50 latency ~18%, but we see a small quality hit on longform/factuality slices (~1.4% absolute on our proxy). looking for recommendation for GTN routing (conservative route, hybrid, or holdback).

alex: can you paste the sample-level breakdown and econ assumptions? e.g. avg tokens/call, billing model, anything product-specific.

maya: pasted the quick table below (from the smoke run). numbers are rough but representative:

```
workload: consumer-chat (multi-turn, summarization-heavy slice)
batch_calls: 100000
avg_tokens_per_call: 210

int8:
  cost_per_call: $0.026
  p50_latency_ms: 120
  p95_latency_ms: 430
  qual_proxy_score: 0.883

int6:
  cost_per_call: $0.017
  p50_latency_ms: 98
  p95_latency_ms: 390
  qual_proxy_score: 0.869

delta_qual = -0.014 absolute (~1.6% relative)
cost_delta = -34.6% per-call
latency_p50_delta = -18%
```

maya: additional notes — on targeted slices (instruction-following, multi-turn factuality), delta_qual is worse: up to -0.033 on small factuality testset. on short single-turn summarization the gap is negligible (~0.004).

rahul: ok — what's the user-visible risk if we route 100% to int6? any examples where hallucination/factuality regressed badly?

maya: a couple of failing examples flagged by eval: hallucinated entity merges in long summaries and degraded citation recall. not catastrophic but visible in our QA regressions. product cares about those slices more.

sophie: could we do a hybrid routing policy? e.g. short queries -> int6, long/multi-turn or flagged recall intents -> int8. we already have prefix-based routing flags in the router.

alex: yep we can route by token-estimate + intent classifier. cost math: if we route 70% calls to int6 and 30% to int8 using the above numbers, weighted cost_per_call = 0.7*0.017 + 0.3*0.026 = $0.02 (approx). that's ~23% saving vs int8-only and likely reduces quality regressions substantially.

maya: propose policy option A/B to present to GTN/product:
- A (aggressive): 80% int6 for single-turn <128 tokens, 20% int8 for multi-turn/recall.
- B (conservative): 60% int6 / 40% int8 + 5% canary/holdback to detect regressions in production.
- C (holdback): default int8, run int6 as 1% shadow for 2w to collect signal.

alex: for product tradeoff framing, compute marginal token-payoff: per-call savings ~ $0.009 -> per-million calls = $9k. if GTN volume is 50M calls/mo, switching 60% yields ~ $270k/mo savings (gross). need to subtract cost of regressions (support + retention) but still meaningful.

sophie: we should also measure latency tail impact on UX (p95 improvement). shorter tails for int6 could help throughput for concurrent users; product may value reduced timeouts.

maya: action plan I propose:
- run a 48h A/B (B policy) with slice-level telemetry enabled (factuality/instruction tags)
- collect 100k routed calls per arm, track qual_proxy + support signals + retention delta
- safety net: automatic fallback to int8 when user reports negative signal or when eval drift > threshold

deploy-bot: :rocket: canary started for 5% traffic -> routing policy B (70/30 by tokens estimated), canary id: cb-lite-int6-4923

rahul: thanks. can you also add a short GTN note with the econ calc and the risk appendix (example failing prompts)? product wants a 1-pager.

maya: will assemble the GTN note and the failing example set. tagging alex and sophie for the econ/ops bits.

alex: i'll update the unit-econ sheet with the hybrid scenario and run the sensitivity curve for avg_tokens in [80,210,500].

sophie: i'll draft the GTN blurb and suggested rollout checklist (canary + escalation path).

maya: cool — let's reconvene after 48h. :eyes:
